question: Which of the following is an intermediate goods industry?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Manufacturing of tools**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **An intermediate good** is an incomplete good that goes as input for further finishing.
 
• Thus, in the production chain, Intermediate goods lie between raw materials and finished goods.
 
• The goods that don't need any more processing are referred to as final goods. These products, usually referred to as consumer goods, are created with the intention of being consumed directly by the final user. The goods that companies utilize to produce goods or services are referred to as intermediate goods.
 
• Since salt is used by producers to create other food products as well as directly consumed by customers, intermediate goods like salt can also be finished goods.
 
• A consumer good, also known as a final good or finished product, is made from an **intermediate item**.
 
• The following are examples of final goods: Items purchased by households are intended for consumption in their whole. For instance, television, milk, prepared meals, medications, and more. It also includes the products that businesses buy to raise funds or for investment purposes.
 
• Hence, the Manufacturing of tools is an example of an intermediate good.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Giffen Goods:

 
 
• A Giffen good is an inferior good with no close substitute available.
 
• Hypothetical example Bread is a good food source for people and when its price increases the people are forced to cut out other eatables like meat and spend more on bread. Hence its demand increases with price.
 
 
 
• Veblen Goods:
 
 
• When the price of goods rises, demand rises as well, and vice versa.
 
• Diamonds, for example, are luxury items whose attraction is based on their high price.
 
• It is named after Thorstein Veblen, an American economist.
 
 
 
• Convenience Goods:
 
 
• Convenience goods are items that are purchased frequently, quickly, and with minimal effort.
 
• These include candy, ice cream, cold drinks, cigarettes, magazines, and medicines, among other things.
 
 
 
• Public Goods:
 
 
• Goods with non-rivalry and non-excludability characteristics, such as national defense are known as public goods.
 
• A public good is a term in economics that refers to the good (commodity) that is available for use for everybody and one person’s usage of it does not diminish or exhaust its availability to others.
 
• Examples of public goods are education, infrastructure, lighthouses, flood control systems, knowledge, fresh air, national security, official statistics, etc.
